sources.title: Influence of Aqueous Stem Bark Extract Terminalia catappa L. on Pregnant Wistar Rats and Brain g-6pdh Activities
sources.limitation: A rat pregnancy experiment with selected fetal measurements and an adult brain enzyme endpoint. It is not evidence of human pregnancy safety, clinical efficacy, a household recipe or a safe human dose. Full-paper quality appraisal was not completed.

sources.title: Phytochemistry and Acute Toxicity Study of Aqueous and Methanol Stem Bark Extract of Terminalia catappa
sources.limitation: Acute rodent toxicity observations do not establish chronic or human safety or a medicinal dose. The paper has wording inconsistencies (leaf versus stem bark; ethanol versus methanol) and differences between dose descriptions and its table; no numerical regimen or blanket safe/non-toxic conclusion is adopted.

proposal.proposedWarnings: The reviewed stem-bark safety studies involved rats, not people. They do not establish a safe human medicinal dose or safety in human pregnancy. Kernel-food processing is separate and does not justify bark or leaf treatment. Human bark safety and contraindications remain unresolved in this review.
proposal.proposedModernEvidenceNote: The reviewed stem-bark studies are rat experiments, including a pregnancy experiment, not human efficacy trials. Their results cannot establish human treatment benefit or a safe medicinal regimen.
publicationBlockers: Human bark and pregnancy safety remains unresolved; these citations are rat studies, not clinical clearance.
